included: One bounded packed public browser SDK consumer using the exact archive below
Normal browser TLS trust, exact CORS origin, credential use, current/history reads and cleanup
excluded: Viewer development, packaging, integration and product-UI acceptance
Installed app/package replacement, LaunchAgent or production service changes
Edge, Home Assistant, vehicle actions, collection and named-source parity
x86, x86_64, amd64, Intel Mac, Azure and full cross-architecture work

local_server.lifecycle: The runner creates the server before the browser connects and closes it in finally after the bounded route. No separate product server is started.

environment.TESLATLAS_BROWSER_CDP_URL: Hub supplies one fresh trusted Chrome CDP endpoint at handoff
environment.TESLATLAS_BROWSER_UNTRUSTED_CDP_URL: Hub supplies one fresh untrusted Chrome CDP endpoint at handoff

browser_controls.trusted: Fresh owner-scoped Chrome profile with the supplied CA installed through normal macOS trust; no TLS bypass flag.
browser_controls.untrusted: Fresh owner-scoped Chrome control without the supplied CA; the same Hub health URL must fail with ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID.
browser_controls.witness: Hub/SDK returns a mode-0600 JSON witness whose trusted and untrusted argument arrays exactly match live CDP command lines and whose exported CA digest matches the fixture CA.

assertions: The exact archive SHA-256, package metadata, 81-member manifest and dist/browser.js hash match before any Hub request.
Trusted browser normal TLS reaches the Hub; untrusted browser control fails closed with ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID.
The browser origin is exactly http://localhost:4174 and at least one Hub CORS preflight is observed.
Public discovery and readiness pass with the expected Hub identity and profile binding.
The fresh owner-prepared credential is accepted; vehicles is nonempty; current state decodes; drive history returns all five rows over 2/2/1 pages.
A conditional drives request returns 304 and the first-page cursor continues successfully after that 304.
Credential rotation and the following default Fetch vehicles request pass.
The SDK local server, trusted/untrusted browser controls and receipt close cleanly; no product listener remains.

allowed_content: localhost origin and CORS preflight count
Hub ID, certificate digest and normal/untrusted trust result
vehicle/drive counts, page shape, 304 and cursor booleans
forbidden_content: invitation bytes, pairing URI or PIN
unredacted browser profile paths beyond declared owner-only metadata

cleanup.hub_scope: Terminate only the fixture launcher after the SDK result or expiry, verify direct Hub-child exit, mode-0600 stopped receipt and closure of 18494.
cleanup.sdk_scope: Stop the local 4174 server and both browser controls, retain only the mode-0600 redacted receipt and remove no unrelated process, trust entry or installed service.
cleanup.credential_policy: Hub and SDK retain private credential/invitation material only under owner-only paths; no secret is copied into the repository or chat.
cleanup.old_input_policy: The closed 18492/18493 runtime tuples, old R2/R4 runtime roots and all prior credentials remain non-reusable; the current 18521 runtime is admissible only because its endpoint, CA, descriptor and credential are fresh.

hub_must_publish: fresh ready descriptor and its SHA-256
fresh CA path, SHA-256 and mode
fresh owner-only credential path and mode
fresh Hub identity, endpoint, process ownership and expiry
trusted/untrusted CDP endpoints and matching mode-0600 launch witness
handoff_acceptance.sdk_must_not_start_before: All Hub-supplied fields above are present and metadata-validated; the SDK proposal itself does not authorize a fixture or browser start.

limits: This proposal is source/package and runner-contract evidence only until Hub publishes the fresh handoff and the SDK produces a redacted receipt.
It is not installed app/package, production, collection, named-source parity, Viewer, Edge, Home Assistant, vehicle or cross-architecture acceptance.
The generic browser helper consumes a caller-owned credential; the proposal does not claim browser-side invitation pairing unless the future runner receipt explicitly records it.
